subject: Energy
title: Floating Offshore Wind
description: A fast breakdown of Floating Offshore Wind for builders.

hook.text: Floating wind turbines sit on platforms anchored to the seabed—accessing deep-water wind beyond fixed foundations.

buildup.text: 80% of offshore wind resources are in deep water (over 60m)—fixed-bottom turbines can't reach these areas.

discovery.text: Hywind Scotland (2017) proved floating wind works—five turbines have operated in the North Sea for years.

twist.text: Floating platforms can be assembled in port and towed out—potentially cheaper and faster than fixed construction.

climax.text: The US, Japan, and South Korea have vast deep-water wind potential—floating tech could unlock gigawatts of capacity.

punchline.text: Float a turbine on the open sea—deep-water wind unlocked.

quiz.question: Why is floating offshore wind important?
options: It accesses deep-water resources fixed turbines can't reach
